title: Malo932: Mario Kart World DLC will feature Star Fox for 2027 and Star Fox Adventure-style game still happening
author: Sickr
content:
A Nintendo leaker with a proven track record Malo932 has said that the eventual Mario Kart World DLC in currently in development and aiming for a 2027 release. That’s not all as Malo932 says that it will feature Star Fox. Talking of Star Fox, Malo932 said that a Star Fox Adventure-inspired title is in deep development at Nintendo, though a release date has not been made clear for this particular title. Malo932 has been casually leaving comments on YouTube videos and his posts have only just become known due to his track record of correctly naming titles which were in development.

title: DLSS 5 reduced the performance of the RTX 5090 from 114 to 60 FPS in 4K in Forza Horizon 6
author: Evgen Kovalov
content:
Experts conducted detailed hardware benchmarking of the NVIDIA DLSS 5 neural network rendering technology in a racing simulator. Forza Horizon 6 at Extreme graphics presets in native 4K resolution with ray tracing enabled. The flagship processor-based configuration was used as a testbed. AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D with a frequency of 5225 MHz, 32 GB of DDR5 RAM with a frequency of 6000 MHz, and a top-of-the-line NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 graphics accelerator. The experts focused primarily on a direct comparison of the video card telemetry before and after activating the cinematic neural network profile.
![Image e4xwihe4xwihe4xw ggpu](https://gamegpu.com/images/1_2026/NEWS/Q3/Sent/Image_e4xwihe4xwihe4xw_g_ggpu.webp)
The benchmark results demonstrated a catastrophic drop in performance for the flagship graphics chip when running heavy post-processing algorithms. Without DLSS 5, the graphics card delivered an average rendering speed of 114 FPS with a frame rate of only 8.6 ms, a core clock of 2820 MHz, and a power consumption of 487.1 W. Enabling DLSS 5 Cinematic mode resulted in an immediate drop in frame rate to 60 FPS, representing a net performance loss of 47%. At the same time, the frame generation time more than doubled to 17.4 ms, rare 1% Low events dropped from 97 FPS to 56 FPS, and 0.1% Low events dropped from 72 FPS to 56 FPS.
![image 90896y7sebtfwftb8wfrynw97fty89wy ggpu](https://gamegpu.com/images/1_2026/NEWS/Q3/Sent/image_90896y7sebtfwftb8wfrynw97fty89wy_g_ggpu.webp)
The colossal computational load from the neural network matrices led to a sharp increase in the operating conditions of the graphics adapter hardware. The graphics card's power consumption increased by 80.3 W and reached an extreme 567.4 W, which led to a rise in the die temperature from 61°C to 67°C and a forced reset of the processor clock rate from 2820 MHz to 2640 MHz. The video buffer remained loaded at 16 GB with a video memory frequency of 14001 MHz, and the GPU utilization increased to a maximum of 99%. Testing clearly demonstrated that, at this stage, the architecture of DLSS 5 algorithms is capable of neutralizing the potential of even the most powerful graphics accelerators on the market.
summary: Experts benchmarked NVIDIA's DLSS 5 technology using Forza Horizon 6 in 4K with ray tracing on a high-end system featuring an RTX 5090. Activating the DLSS 5 Cinematic mode caused a catastrophic 47% performance drop, reducing the frame rate from 114 FPS to 60 FPS. The heavy computational load also increased power consumption to 567.4 W, raised the GPU temperature to 67°C, and lowered the core clock rate to 2640 MHz.
key_points: Enabling DLSS 5 Cinematic mode reduced performance from 114 FPS to 60 FPS in native 4K with ray tracing.
Frame generation time more than doubled from 8.6 ms to 17.4 ms.
Power consumption increased by 80.3 W to reach an extreme 567.4 W.
GPU temperature rose from 61°C to 67°C, forcing a clock rate reduction from 2820 MHz to 2640 MHz.

title: Maldon gardener's giant pumpkin to compete at RHS show
author: Jessica Ure
content:
![Ben White wears a dark-coloured T-shirt, and black sunglasses, standing behind a giant orange and wrinkled pumpkin. He is inside a tent.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/5b7c/live/e424ed80-a888-11f1-96fc-dd627484b0e6.jpg)
Ben White and Gladys will compete at the RHS Malvern Autumn Show over the last weekend of September
- Published
An amateur gardener is nurturing his giant pumpkin in preparation for an RHS competition later this month.
Ben White, from Maldon in Essex, has grown his biggest pumpkin to date weighing about 1,200lb (544kg) - and still growing.
The 37-year-old is documenting the rise of the mighty vegetable, named Gladys, on social media, to raise money for the Essex & Herts Air Ambulance charity.
Gladys will compete at the RHS Malvern Autumn Show over the last weekend of September.
Even though the weight of his pumpkin is similar to that of a small car, it is less than half the weight of the Guinness World Record title holder.
Twins Stuart and Ian Paton, from Lymington in Hampshire, claimed that honour in October 2025 with a giant pumpkin weighing 2,819lb (1,278kg).
![Ben White kneels beside a giant yellow pumpkin. He wears blue shorts and a T-shirt, wearing black sunglasses. There are green plants around him in soil.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1440/cpsprodpb/96cb/live/e578ef20-a864-11f1-ae45-e9984fc27c77.png)
Gladys, pictured in its more juvenile years, has been carefully grown
Gladys was pollinated on 30 June and at her peak was growing 40lb (18kg) a day.
Months of preparation, studying irrigation, and carefully controlled water and nutrition went into growing the giant vegetable.
White works as an underfloor heating designer, but grows vegetables inside a 60ft (18m) polytunnel at a local farm in his spare time.
He also grows tomatoes, peppers, chillies, watermelons and sweet potatoes to avoid having to rely heavily on supermarkets.
"There is something incredibly satisfying about walking on to the plot and bringing home food you've grown yourself," said White.
In 2021 he became the first grower to showcase a giant pumpkin inside the Great Pavilion at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show.
Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.
summary: Amateur gardener Ben White from Maldon, Essex, has grown a giant pumpkin named Gladys weighing about 1,200lb (544kg). The pumpkin will compete at the RHS Malvern Autumn Show during the last weekend of September. White is also using his social media documentation of the vegetable to raise money for the Essex & Herts Air Ambulance charity.
key_points: Ben White's giant pumpkin, Gladys, weighs approximately 1,200lb and is still growing.
Gladys will compete at the RHS Malvern Autumn Show in late September.
White is documenting the pumpkin's growth on social media to raise funds for the Essex & Herts Air Ambulance.
Gladys was pollinated on June 30 and grew up to 40lb a day at her peak.
White previously became the first grower to showcase a giant pumpkin inside the Great Pavilion at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in 2021.

title: Is it Finally Time for 3D Mario? 14 Predictions for the September 2026 Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct
author: Logan Plant
content:
Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days, and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement. On Tuesday, September 8, it’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a more general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9. You can read up on how to watch both Nintendo Direct presentations here. But while we wait, it's predictions time!
Before we start, a couple of disclaimers: these are all purely my guesses based on public information and my analysis of Nintendo’s release patterns, and nothing more. Nothing here is based on any inside information. But, I will be discussing a couple of relevant leaks over the last few months, so if you have been steering clear of information like that, you may not want to read on.
Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Predictions
Zelda is my favorite series, so I’m buzzing thinking about all the possibilities we could see Tuesday morning. But I’m trying to keep things realistic in this piece and only sharing predictions that I think have a legitimate chance of happening.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Full Reveal
This will undoubtedly be the centerpiece of the presentation. We’ve only seen a few seconds of footage of the Ocarina of Time remake, which is set to come out in 2026. So, now’s the time for the full reveal trailer and release date. I can’t wait for this one; my imagination has been running wild over this remake for the last three months, and we’re finally going to see more about the scope of this remake. Is it faithful, or more of a reimagining? What does the kingdom of Hyrule look like beyond Link’s treehouse? All that and more will likely be answered by a more conventional trailer that gives us a proper look at the remake.
I don’t know exactly what Ocarina of Time will look like, but the teaser trailer from earlier this year tells me Nintendo is very confident in this game. You don’t set the internet’s imagination on fire with a 10-second tease of Link’s treehouse if you don’t have really satisfying answers to share when you do finally pull the curtain back, and I expect the Ocarina of Time remake to be a pretty big deal.
Ocarina of Time's Release Date
As for a release date, I’m expecting Ocarina of Time to arrive on Thursday, November 12. Nintendo doesn’t have a game dated for November yet (Fire Emblem arrives this month, with Nintendo Switch Sports slated for October), and it never misses putting out a big game in the weeks before Black Friday. Knowing it’s coming this year, Zelda feels primed for that spot. Nintendo is extremely unlikely to release a game on Thanksgiving (that’s Thursday, November 26 in the U.S.), and it has no reason to go head-to-head with Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19. That just leaves November 5 and 12 as available Thursdays to launch a game. A few weeks back, the Nintendo UK store briefly dated a couple of Kirby Air Riders amiibo for November 12, and Nintendo typically launches amiibo the same day as a first-party game, even if the franchises aren’t related. That date has since been removed, but I’m still pretty locked in on November 12 as Ocarina of Time’s release date.
Ocarina of Time amiibo
With amiibo on the mind, I’m hopeful we’ll get a glimpse of a new amiibo line for Ocarina of Time alongside the reveal. Zelda games typically get tie-in amiibo figures (Echoes of Wisdom is a rare recent exception), so I’m expecting we’ll see figures of Young Link and Adult Link at the very least.
Special Edition Nintendo Switch 2 and Pro Controller
A few weeks ago, allegedly leaked designs surfaced for a Zelda-themed Nintendo Switch 2 console and Pro Controller. These don’t appear to be branded for Ocarina of Time specifically, but rather for the 40th anniversary as a whole. If they’re legitimate, it'd make the most sense to see the products formally announced on Tuesday, potentially alongside my predicted November 12 release for Ocarina of Time. And if they don’t show up, you can pretty confidently write that leak off as fake. Right now, my gut says they’re real and will show up.
The Legend of Zelda Movie News
The Legend of Zelda movie hits theaters next April, and aside from casting news and a few official teaser images from Nintendo, we haven’t seen anything from the film. It’s become common for Shigeru Miyamoto to show up to present Mario movie news in Directs, so it seems very likely that he’ll do the same here. I think we could get official casting news for Ganondorf and other characters that have been reported on in recent weeks, and I bet we’ll see a short clip, too, if not a full trailer.
The Zelda Challenge
In June, Nintendo unveiled the DK Challenge: a series of time-limited challenges tied to Donkey Kong Bananza and classic DK games available on Nintendo Switch Online. It’s Nintendo’s experimental take on achievements or trophies, and notably, the DK Challenge just ended earlier this week. Based on the way it was integrated into Switch 2’s OS, this concept doesn’t seem like a one-off, and I can’t think of a better choice to follow it up than holding the Zelda Challenge for the franchise’s 40th anniversary. I’m not sure what modern game would be tied into this – maybe Breath of the Wild? – but this seems like a good way to build hype for the milestone year while encouraging fans to revisit classic Zeldas in the weeks leading up to Ocarina of Time.
Twilight Princess on Nintendo Switch Online
Speaking of NSO, it bothers me more than it should that The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess is the only 3D Zelda game that’s not playable in some form on Switch 2. Its excellent soundtrack isn’t available on the Nintendo Music app either, which strikes me as odd. I think Nintendo will right both of these wrongs on Tuesday, by shadowdropping the GameCube version of Twilight Princess on Nintendo Switch Online and adding its music to the app shortly after. Twilight Princess turns 20 years old in just a couple of months, so now seems like the perfect time.
The Return of Multiplayer Zelda
The Zelda Direct is 30 minutes long, so I think there’s time for one more game announcement in addition to everything I’ve already discussed. If I’m putting this presentation together, though, I don’t really want to overshadow Ocarina of Time with anything too big. With that said, I think the time is right for the return of a multiplayer Zelda game. Nintendo hasn’t put out a multiplayer-focused Zelda game since 2015’s Tri Force Heroes on 3DS, and neither it nor the Four Swords games are available on Switch or Switch 2.
It’s a more niche corner of the franchise that’s been neglected for some time, and there are a few ways a multiplayer surprise could go down. We could get the “Zelda 99” battle royale treatment we’ve seen applied to classic games like Tetris, F-Zero, Pac-Man, and even Super Mario Bros. for its 35th anniversary. Or, it could be an NSO rerelease of the Game Boy Advance’s Four Swords, or the GameCube’s Four Swords Adventures, either of which could hugely benefit from online multiplayer support. Of course, it could be a brand new game in the style of past co-op Zeldas, but that feels the least likely. No matter what form it takes, I’m ready to see multiplayer Zelda return in the Direct.
The Next Main Zelda Reveal?
The core 3D Zelda team – led by Director Hidemaro Fujibayashi and longtime series producer Eiji Aonuma – are no doubt hard at work on their followup to 2023’s Tears of the Kingdom. The question is, will we see it on Tuesday? I’m inclined to guess we won’t. Ocarina of Time is the big Zelda story right now, and even a glimpse of what’s next might take away from the conversation surrounding the remake. If it does show, though, I don’t think it’d be any more than the smallest of teases. We’re talking five to 10 seconds of Link looking over a hill. But I’m not holding my breath. Especially with another general Nintendo Direct the following day, there’s no need to fire the open-world Zelda cannon at this point in the Switch 2’s life.
My Pie-in-the-Sky Dream: The 8-bit Breath of the Wild Prototype Is Released
I said all of my predictions were meant to have a solid chance of happening, but this one’s just for me. While exploring early concepts that would lead to the development of Breath of the Wild, the Zelda team built a playable, 8-bit prototype to test their ideas. It demonstrated ideas like chopping down trees to cross rivers and fire spreading across a grassy field, set in a Hyrule reminiscent of the NES original. It wasn’t meant to be a commercial product, but how cool would it be if Nintendo dropped it on Switch as part of the anniversary celebrations? I think the odds of this happening are essentially zero, but I’d love nothing more than to have access to a playable piece of Breath of the Wild’s development history.
General Nintendo Direct Predictions
That’s just day one! On Wednesday, September 9, Nintendo is airing its general Direct, featuring 45 minutes of updates on Nintendo Switch 2 games. This one is particularly exciting for different reasons: the Zelda Direct is presumably all about getting answers to our Ocarina of Time questions, while we have no idea what the centerpiece of the Wednesday show will be.
Updates on the 2026/2027 Slate
Much of the runtime will likely go to final updates and trailers on Nintendo games still set to come out this year. Expect last looks at Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave (out September 17) and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (October 22), as well as updates on Pokémon Pokopia’s next waves of DLC.
We could also get another look at Xenoblade Genesis, Monolith Soft’s next RPG that’s due out in 2027. Something I’m not expecting to see is Pokémon Winds & Waves, though. It’s also set for next year, but given that mainline Pokémon games typically release in the Fall, I’m not expecting to see the next generation show up again until a Pokémon Presents showcase in February 2027 at the earliest.
The Duskbloods Release Date
Following its network test last month, I think we’ll get a release date for FromSoftware’s The Duskbloods. The Nintendo Store still lists it as a 2026 game, and December is feeling the most likely to me right now. Nintendo is publishing The Duskbloods outside of Japan. If you follow the pattern of Nintendo typically publishing one game a month, and you accept my reasoning that Ocarina is the November game, the only month left for The Duskbloods to theoretically land in is December. Purely to get a guess on the record, I’ll predict Thursday, December 3, mostly for the reason that when Nintendo does publish a game in December, it’s generally pretty early in the month, like Metroid Prime 4: Beyond on December 4 last year.
2D Metroid Reveal
On the topic of Metroid, it’s time to see MercurySteam’s next entry in the 2D Metroid series. The studio released Samus Returns on 3DS in 2017 and Dread on Switch in 2021, so it feels like we’re due for a new one in 2027. There was a recent video game age rating leak out of Brazil for a submission titled “Metroid Ravenous”. That leak featured no details other than the name, so there’s still a lot up in the air. However, Dread’s main villain was named Raven Beak, making “Ravenous” a pretty intriguing title for a potential sequel. Nintendo has been revealing new games fairly close to their release dates over the last few years, so I wouldn’t be surprised to see Metroid Ravenous announced on Wednesday and released as early as Q1 of 2027.
The Big Finale
There’s been this itch in the back of my brain all day. Nintendo has never aired back-to-back Directs in this way on two consecutive days. In other years, they’ve just glued the Mario 40th Anniversary segment onto a larger Nintendo Direct. I find the order peculiar, too. If the Zelda Direct blows us away (which I’m expecting Ocarina of Time to), why isn’t that one airing second as the big endcap to the week? Ocarina of Time has the power to close out a show, but it’s probably not going to be a factor on Wednesday. This tells me Nintendo must have something pretty special to end its second Direct with. Something big that won’t launch until the second half of 2027, but the announcement alone will help fuel Switch 2 sales through the holiday season. The two things I can think of that fit the bill are either Super Smash Bros. or the next 3D Super Mario. I think we’ll see one – not both – of these announced at the end of Wednesday’s show.
I can see arguments for each: I predicted a Super Smash Bros. Ultimate - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition at the start of the year. Here’s what I said in January that I still feel today:
“My boldest call of them all is that we’ll get a tease this year for Super Smash Bros. Ultimate - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition to launch sometime in 2027. I believe Ultimate could get the Mario Kart 8 Deluxe treatment this generation, with an enhanced port that carries us through the next several years rather than an entirely new entry. Smash Bros. director Masahiro Sakurai wrapped up Kirby Air Riders a few months ago, and it’s entirely possible he’s already hard at work bringing Ultimate over to Switch 2 with a few new characters. Ultimate noticeably hasn’t received a Switch 2 performance patch like Super Mario Odyssey, the open-world Zeldas, and plenty of other best-selling Switch 1 games, and combined with the fact that a new Smash game almost always hits within the first two years of a new Nintendo console, it feels like a prime candidate for a Switch 2 Edition.”
And, after spending the last year declaring it to be too soon for 3D Mario in the wake of Donkey Kong Bananza – another 3D mascot platformer from much of the same team as 3D Mario – I now think we’re entering the window where we could see the plumber show up any time. The Bananza marketing cycle is winding down: the DK Challenge just ended on NSO, the Emerald Rush DLC has gone through an entire year of limited-time events, and by the time 2027 rolls around, Bananza will have had two full holiday seasons as the primary platformer on Switch 2. I think Mario’s time is coming.
My Dream: Ace Attorney 7
This is one of my favorite series, and I predict it every time. It has to happen at some point!
Those are my predictions for the pair of Nintendo Directs airing over the next few days. I can’t wait to cover it all here on IGN and Nintendo Voice Chat. Be sure to drop your own predictions in the comments!
Logan Plant is the host of Nintendo Voice Chat and IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and DB. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero. You can find new episodes of NVC every Friday on the IGN Games YouTube channel, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your favorite podcast app.
summary: Nintendo is hosting two consecutive presentations: a Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct on September 8 followed by a general Nintendo Direct on September 9. Predictions for the Zelda Direct include a full reveal and a November release date for the Ocarina of Time remake, tie-in amiibo, and potential NSO additions. The general Direct is expected to feature updates on upcoming 2026 and 2027 software slates, release dates for titles like The Duskbloods, and potential new game announcements.
key_points: Nintendo is holding a Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct on Tuesday, September 8, and a general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9.
The author predicts a full reveal and a November 12 release date for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
Other Zelda predictions include a potential Zelda-themed Switch 2 console, movie news, and Twilight Princess arriving on Nintendo Switch Online.
The general Nintendo Direct is expected to showcase updates on 2026 and 2027 games, including Fire Emblem, Pokémon DLC, and a release date for The Duskbloods.

title: These 20+ Games Are Coming To Xbox Next Week (September 7-11)
author: Pure Xbox; Fraser Gilbert
content:
Welcome to your Xbox games roundup for September 7-11! We've got a few big releases on the way over the next few days including Halloween: The Game, Mewgenics and EA Sports NHL 27, while Xbox Game Pass is treating us to three new additions highlighted by Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War!
Here's what's coming to Xbox next week:
New Xbox Releases (September 7-11)
- Bus Simulator 27 (September 8): "Whether you are interested in classic rigid, articulated, and double-decker buses or in new electric buses – Bus Simulator 27 has got you covered."
- Culdcept The First Saturn Tribute (September 8): "The original Culdcept was released in 1997; a combination of digital board game and deck building, it saw numerous sequels, but that very first game never left Japan, until now!"
- Halloween: The Game (September 8): "Take The Shape of Evil as Michael Myers or save your neighbors as a Hero of Haddonfield in Halloween, the ultimate asymmetrical horror sandbox."
- Hole in Many (September 8): "Get ready to put your aim and logic to the test in Hole in Many, a fun puzzle game that combines the strategy of moving pieces with the excitement of golf."
- Honeycomb: The World Beyond (September 8): "Harness your bioengineering knowledge and make use of the extensive training provided by EON to navigate a world brimming with wonders and mysteries."
- Mewgenics (September 8): Draft abilities, collect items, and manipulate genetics across generations in this roguelike tactics game from the creators of The Binding of Isaac and The End is Nigh.
- SPRAWL zero (September 8): "Sprawl Zero is a first-person shooter inspired by 2000s console FPS games. Both the aesthetics and design sensibility call back to the Golden Age where the genre evolved from shooting in corridors to building worlds."
- Barbarian Saga: The Beastmaster (September 9): "Barbarian Saga: The Beastmaster will transport you to a future land of magic and sword, make your way through this action Metroidvania and discover with your Heart-Eater sword an epic outcome in a decadent world where they want to eradicate all non-human creatures."
- Cats Around Us: Black Cats (September 9): "Cats Around Us: Black Cat is the second part of the series where you search for hidden furballs inside a five-page silent comic."
- Jewel Match Solitaire X (September 9): "Play more than 500 levels, including the new Sliding level type, while unlocking classic and additional solitaire variants such as Carlton, Fanny, or Daisy Garden!"
- BrokenLore: DON'T LIE (September 10): "BrokenLore: DON’T LIE is a Japanese psychological horror game exploring trauma, isolation, and a fractured reality where perception becomes increasingly unreliable."
- Deconstruction Simulator (September 10): "Deconstruction Simulator is the ultimate demolition simulator, offering you complete freedom of action and a wide array of contracts to complete. Get ready for spectacular destruction."
- Dumb Ways To Build (September 10): "Dumb Ways to Build is a physics-based co-op game filled with deadly construction jobs that no sane crew would touch."
- Fresh Tracks (September 10): "Will you unite the splintered pantheon of Norwyn to defeat Mar, the Queen of Terror? Fight, jump, and dodge obstacles and menacing enemies as you ski further into the darkness that has befallen the snow-covered land of Norwyn."
- HOT WHEELS™ Infinite Rush (September 10): "Race beyond the orange track and jump into a Hot Wheels™-sized world with four islands to explore, each with its own vibe and challenges."
- Lost in Loss (September 10): "Explore beautiful hand-drawn locations, search for unusual hidden objects, and uncover the secrets behind each person’s story."
- Mole Mine Boom (September 10): "Get ready to venture deep underground in Mole Mine Boom, a fun logic puzzle where every move can completely transform the path ahead."
- RIN: The Last Child (September 10): "Play as RIN, the last child of the Creator, on a journey to restore balance to a broken world. Craft powerful spells, collect magical aspects and runes, and confront your transformed siblings in intense boss battles where every choice matters."
- The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline (September 10): "There is no combat; only the tension of the unknown. Immerse yourself in a dark, modern interpretation of the Divine Comedy, where the Inferno is a shadow waiting to consume you."
- The Royal Writ (September 10): "In The Royal Writ, you don’t just play cards – you command them on the battlefield. Place your loyal subjects strategically as they advance toward the enemy, dealing damage."
- Train Sim World® 7: Deluxe Edition (September 10): "Find Your Way in Train Sim World 7! Embark on a new journey as you explore 3 iconic routes aboard an array of easy to learn, hard to master locomotives:"
- Warshift 2: Machines of Madness (September 10): "Warshift 2: Machines of Madness is a unique mix of Strategy, Action, and RPG gameplay elements."
- Dino Odyssey (September 11): "In Dino Odyssey, you control a brave dinosaur on a dangerous journey to rescue the eggs of your kind, ensuring the survival and birth of new generations. Run, jump, and use your wits to explore a world full of threats."
- Dominus Mahjong Arcana (September 11): "With 40 carefully designed levels and progressively increasing difficulty, the game offers a smooth and relaxing journey suitable for players of all ages."
- EA Sports NHL 27 (September 11): "EA SPORTS™ NHL® 27 brings the identity of every NHL team to life on the ice, in the arena, and through the broadcast."
- Liquid Cats (September 11): "Liquid Cats: Cozy Line Puzzle is a warm, one-line logic game with one wonderfully simple goal: guide a stretchy cat across the grid and fill every empty tile."
Xbox Game Pass Titles
- Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War (September 8)
- The Royal Writ (September 10)
- Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage (September 10)
summary: Over twenty new games are scheduled for release on Xbox between September 7 and September 11. Highlighted titles launching during the week include Halloween: The Game, Mewgenics, and EA Sports NHL 27. Additionally, Xbox Game Pass is adding three new titles, led by Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War.
key_points: More than 20 games are releasing for Xbox between September 7 and September 11.
Notable new releases include Halloween: The Game, Mewgenics, and EA Sports NHL 27.
Xbox Game Pass is receiving three new additions during the week.
Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War headlines the new Xbox Game Pass arrivals.

title: There May Not Be an iPhone 18 This Year
author: Boone Ashworth
content:
Every year around this time, Apple announces new iPhones. The products go on sale soon after, usually ranging from a base model to more premium and more expensive Pro models. But this year will likely be different—not just because the company has a brand-new CEO.
Apple’s iPhone event will be held on September 9 at 10 am Pacific (1 pm Eastern), announced last week with the title “Surprise and Shine!” If you tune into the livestream, expect the announcement of an iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and, if all the rumors and widely held analyst expectations are true, the first look at an Apple foldable device.
Based on leaks and the ongoing tech rumor mill and its decent track record for figuring these things out, Apple is expected to prioritize its more expensive, premium devices this year and hold off on announcing its base model iPhone 18. That cheaper model is rumored to launch in the spring of 2027, potentially alongside an iPhone 18e and maybe a second-generation iPhone Air.
Why the drastic change in strategy? It may be due to the ongoing memory shortage, which has made just about everything more expensive. Apple hasn’t been spared. In June, former Apple CEO Tim Cook acknowledged that Apple would raise product prices to keep up with manufacturing costs.
“Our assumption is that they're going to be launching three models in the fall, the premium side of the models of the 18 series,” says Nabila Popal, a senior director of data and analytics at IDC. “Then the mid/budget devices will be launched in the spring.”
Popal says it's a smart strategic move because Apple is aiming to spread out its revenue between a usually very strong fourth quarter and a typically much weaker spring quarter the following year. Apple’s portfolio has also expanded, and the iPhone Pro and Pro Max lineup are more enticing for people already prepared to spend the money on a new iPhone.
When components become more expensive, companies have three real options: Eat the costs, raise prices, or, as Apple seems to be doing, lean into it. By moving its cheaper options to a later date, Apple can drum up excitement for its bigger, better, pricier offerings. When it charges more for those, it is likely to be less off-putting than making a cheap phone even more expensive. It’s part of a “premiumization” of devices, as Popal calls it, that Apple hopes to leverage and build hype for its pricier options.
Shawn DuBravac, chief economist at the Global Electronics Association, tells WIRED he is optimistic about what these kinds of rising prices ultimately mean for customers.
“Throughout the history of time, the deflationary pressures of technology have always flowed to the consumer,” DuBravac says. “I'm confident that will be the case again. It just will take some time for the markets to solidify.” In other words, new technologies launch with a high price, but manufacturing efficiencies and competition inevitably drive costs down for consumers.
That may not be the case anytime soon for folding phones, which are seeing higher prices than ever. Samsung’s entire 2026 Galaxy Z folding smartphone range saw price increases, as did Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and Motorola’s Razr 2026 models. Apple’s folding iPhone is rumored to cost around $2,000.
To help mitigate those high costs, Apple is turning to financing options and trade-in programs. In July, the company launched an iPhone leasing program that lets people pay a monthly fee to rent the newest iPhones, then swap them out when a new device releases. The program will undoubtedly help more people afford the newest devices, but ownership advocates have criticized it, saying it keeps you from truly owning and managing your device. It also fits Apple’s broader effort to turn all of its products into a subscription service.
“The way most consumers buy Apple phones is through financing or trade-in programs,” Popal says. “We can expect a lot more aggressive trade-ins to help cushion that.”
Thanks to the memory crisis and price increases, all smartphones are getting more costly to make. Less expensive phones become less appealing for manufacturers to prioritize, and leading smartphone brands have started to see them as far less economical to produce.
On the flip side, demand for refurbished devices has been climbing for a while now, with sales of used devices growing even as new phone sales slow down. More people are looking to save money or purchase more eco-friendly products.
“The days of the cheap smartphone are over,” Popal says.
summary: Apple's upcoming September 9 event is expected to feature the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and potentially its first foldable device, while delaying the base model iPhone 18 to spring 2027. This shift in strategy is driven by an ongoing memory shortage and rising manufacturing costs, leading Apple to prioritize premium devices and spread out its revenue across quarters. To help customers afford these more expensive products, Apple is increasingly relying on financing options, leasing programs, and trade-ins.
key_points: Apple may skip releasing a base model iPhone 18 this fall, holding it and other mid-tier devices for a spring 2027 launch.
An ongoing memory shortage and higher manufacturing costs are driving Apple to focus on premium devices like the iPhone 18 Pro and a rumored foldable phone.
Apple is utilizing aggressive trade-ins, financing, and a new leasing program to help consumers manage rising smartphone prices.
Demand for refurbished devices is growing as new smartphone sales slow down and manufacturing costs make cheap phones less economical to produce.

title: Marvel's Venom Still in Dev for PS5, Will Surely Be Huge
author: Push Square; Sammy Barker
content:
![Marvel's Venom Still in Dev for PS5, Will Surely Be Huge 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/369d4f5542d71/marvels-venom-still-in-dev-for-ps5-will-surely-be-huge-1.900x.jpg)
Insomniac is still working on its previously rumoured Marvel’s Venom game, according to dependable industry snoop NatetheHate2.
The unfortunately named leaker has accurately outed a number of projects over the years, and says Sony studio Insomniac is very much still beavering away on this spin-off.
It follows comments from Bloomberg’s equally dependable Jason Schreier, who ruled out rumours the title had been cancelled earlier in the year.
Word of a Venom game first emerged in the infamous Insomniac leak, where it was listed on a roadmap of upcoming releases. While timelines have shifted since then, it seems like this game is still very much on the agenda.
NatetheHate2 says he doesn’t know when this project will be announced, but I’d personally expect it to be a cross-gen title on both the PS6 and PS5 – perhaps as a launch game for the new console like Marvel’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales.
It makes sense that Sony hasn’t acknowledged it yet because all of its marketing efforts are focused on Marvel’s Wolverine right now, which is out imminently.
Personally, I think a well-executed Venom game has the potential to be massive, as the character is ridiculously popular. All of the Tom Hardy movies did pretty well, despite them receiving rough reviews.
Are you down for more Marvel from Insomniac, or are you reaching fatigue with superhero stuff now? Suppress your inner-symbiote in the comments section below.
summary: Insomniac is actively developing the rumored Marvel's Venom game for PlayStation platforms. Industry sources confirm the project remains in production, dismissing earlier rumors of its cancellation. Sony has not yet officially announced the game as marketing efforts currently focus on Marvel's Wolverine.
key_points: Insomniac is still developing the Marvel's Venom spin-off game.
Industry sources like NatetheHate2 and Jason Schreier confirm the project has not been cancelled.
The game was initially revealed through a previous roadmap leak from Insomniac.
Sony is currently focusing its marketing efforts on the upcoming Marvel's Wolverine title.

title: Lenovo goes MacBook Neo: Hands-on review with Lenovo's best-looking $699 laptop
author: Benjamin Herzig
content:
There have been many claimants for the title of MacBook Neo competitor. The great success of Apple's most affordable MacBook laptop has certainly rocked the market in 2026, with the PC manufacturers not really being able to immediately respond.
A few months later, it seems like the big fish of the laptop world have found their footing again. Although it is maybe unfair to attribute everything to the Neo, as product development cycles are typically measured in years, not months, the emergence of more budget friendly systems with attractive is likely less than a coincidence.
Case in point: The new Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe that Lenovo has unveiled at IFA 2026 in Berlin. This new laptop series will be available in 14- and 15-inch, and it sports one of the most interesting designs of the IFA laptop crop. We were able to have some hands-on time with the 14-inch version.
Colors, keys and aluminum: Expressive Lenovo laptop design
One problem many affordable Windows laptops have: they feel cheap. This is something that the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe mostly avoids, by utilizing aluminum for the screen and bottom cover. The laptop feels solid, and even the plastic palmrest does not feel cheap. Plus, the hinges allow single-handed opening.
Of course, Lenovo also had to make compromises to reach the attractive $700 price point. There is a version with a plastic bottom cover instead, and while there is a backlit keyboard, a feature that the MacBook Neo does not offer, it is only optional.
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe 14 in Radiant Coral with custom colored key-caps.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/d/d/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson2_6724313030.jpg)
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe 14 in Moody Blue.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/4/a/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson7_e09d1c010c.jpg)
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe 14 in Chill Blue.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/3/5/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson8_0058c83c2b.jpg)
![Colored keycap sets for the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/f/c/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson4_92b2e18fc9.jpg)
![Keycap removal tool for the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/d/8/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson3_b0b81efddf.jpg)
The 1.35 mm travel keyboard is also the focus in another way, as Lenovo takes the colorful design to the next level here. The IdeaPad Vibe will be available in seven colors, but Lenovo will also offer color-matching keyboard keys. This will enable users to customize the look of their laptop, as the keys are made to be removable.
At the product demo, Lenovo demonstrated how to remove the keys with a special tool, which is included if you buy a set of colorful keyboard keys. We tried to remove the keys without it, but it is not possible, as least not without long fingernails. According to Lenovo, it will also be possible to customize the keyboard colors when buying the IdeaPad Vibe. Sadly though, Lenovo is not going to sell single keycaps, so if you want a certain color, you have to buy the whole set.
AMD and Qualcomm now, Intel Wildcat Lake in the future
Lenovo will launch the IdeaPad Vibe with AMD Ryzen AI CPUs, as well as Qualcomm Snapdragon X chips, but this will not be the whole lineup. The product managers at the IFA event confirmed that a version with Intel's budget-oriented Wildcat Lake CPUs is also planned.
When this version launches, it seems like a natural fit for this affordable laptop series. It will bring a notable limitation, though: Lenovo touts the IdeaPad laptop for its upgradeability. Indeed, it has two SO-DIMM and two M.2 2242 SSD slots. That, however, is only true for the AMD model, as the Qualcomm IdeaPad will ship with soldered RAM. And since Intel Wildcat Lake only supports single-channel RAM, Lenovo would probably reduce the IdeaPads to a single SO-DIMM slot.
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe: Upgradeable internals.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/0/9/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson6_814794b886.jpg)
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe: Left-side ports.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/d/6/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson9_6e655b8e31.jpg)
![Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe: Right-side ports.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/7/c/csm_Lenovo_IdeaPadVibe_handson10_570a51dc57.jpg)
In any case, versatility is certainly the big advantage of the IdeaPad Vibe over the Apple MacBook Neo. With multiple USB ports and HDMI, as well as its upgradeability, the IdeaPad Vibe is by far more usable than the limited MacBook, even going as far as including a microSD card reader.
To us, that seems to be the right mix against the Apple device: Keep the advantages of the PC world - versatility and upgradeability, giving the user choice - while also going for a fresh, more premium design language in the lower price tier.
Source(s)
Own
summary: Lenovo unveiled the new IdeaPad Vibe laptop series at IFA 2026, targeting the budget market with a starting price of $699. Available in 14- and 15-inch sizes, the laptop features an expressive design with up to seven colors and removable, customizable keycaps. It offers various processor options including AMD Ryzen AI, Qualcomm Snapdragon X, and future Intel Wildcat Lake chips, while maintaining strong versatility and upgradeability compared to competitors.
key_points: The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe was unveiled at IFA 2026 with a starting price of $699.
It features an aluminum screen and bottom cover, with an optional backlit keyboard and single-handed opening hinges.
Users can customize the laptop's look using seven available colors and interchangeable, color-matching keycap sets.
The laptop will launch with AMD Ryzen AI and Qualcomm Snapdragon X chips, with future Intel Wildcat Lake models planned.
The AMD model offers high upgradeability with two SO-DIMM and two M.2 2242 SSD slots, alongside multiple ports including USB, HDMI, and a microSD card reader.

title: Unmissable JDM all-stars | Six of the Best
author: Matt Bird
content:
Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VII RS, 2001, 10k, £49,990
The cars of the Japanese Domestic Market have a long and rich history in the UK. Back in the 90s, grey imports - there’s a phrase nobody’s used for a while - established themselves over here. A weak yen coincided with the time of incredible cars, meaning the desirability was encouraged by financial viability. Magazines, motorsport and Gran Turismo introduced many to the joys of the JDM, and the enthusiasm was such that official UK imports of cars like Evos and Skylines began around the millennium. The manufacturers were missing out by not catering to demand. The best versions were still limited to Japanese sales, however, and still are to this day (looking at you, Toyota). Both classics and contemporary creations remain highly prized - this Evo VII RS is the perfect example. The stripped-out Evo was deemed too hardcore for us puny Brits, and never officially sold here. Now it looks like the Lancer at its purest, rawest and most exhilarating. With just 10k miles, it’s for sale at £50k. 
Subaru Impreza STI Type RA NBR Challenge, 2013, 17k, £44,985
But if you were always more Team Subaru than Mitsubishi, then take a look at this. Following the old adage that the longer a JDM name is, the cooler the car, we give you the Impreza STI tS Type RA NBR Challenge. And even by silly Subaru standards, it’s a very special thing. Celebrating race success at the Nurburgring, the Type RA benefitted from new steering, suspension and brakes to make it even sharper than standard; just 200 cars were made in NBR Challenge spec, bringing the carbon aero bits, Recaro seats and forged BBS wheels. Some car, then, with that legendary EJ20 under the bonnet as well. The ad suggests the NBR is considered to be  ‘the greatest incarnation of Impreza ever produced’ - high praise indeed. That’s gotta be worth Golf R money to somebody, hasn’t it? Especially with fewer than 20,000 miles. 
Toyota Supra RZ-S, 1996, 102k, £68,000
Perhaps no car has enjoyed quite such a transformation in image over the past 30 years than the A80 Toyota Supra - with games, films and races all playing a part. What was once offered in the UK as a Porsche 928 rival - a long-legged, luxurious GT loaded with kit - became the world’s most famous tuner car. The 2JZ twin-turbo six became as famous as the car itself, forming the base of epic thousand-horsepower builds; Castrol-liveried Supras romped around Japanese touring cars, and it was perfectly cast in Fast & Furious. Perhaps nothing encapsulates the fascination with all things JDM like an imported Supra. Which you’ll now have to pay handsomely for the privilege of owning: this one is almost £70k with more than 100,000 miles. But it’s had a lot spent in recent years, and the Supra obsession shows no signs of going anywhere. Just be prepared to spend a lot more if you owe somebody a 10-second car. 
Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32), 1990, 27k, £59,995
A bit like Impreza and Evo, you can’t mention the Supra without also mentioning the Skyline. But unlike the Toyota, the Nissan’s legacy was secured well within its own lifetime, the original R32 GT-R utterly dominant in Group A motorsport. You don’t get the Godzilla nickname without some truly crushing successes. The RB26 under the bonnet here is just as loved as the 2JZ, and just as tuneable; while stock is what the collectors want these days, it’s always nice to be reminded of exactly what could be achieved. So here’s an R32 originally built by JUN Auto, with further upgrades since import, making almost the power of an Aston Martin Vanquish. More than 800hp for less than £60k is the main appeal here, with a rare colour and miniscule mileage also in its favour. Plus, well, it’s a R32 GT-R on a set of TE37s and with Bride seats - it could hardly look better. 
Mazda Eunos Roadster S-Special, 1993, 73k, £11,995
There are affordable JDM heroes out there as well - you just need to know where to look. Imported MX-5s (or Eunos Roadsters, to be accurate) have always appealed, typically offering more equipment for less money than a UKDM equivalent. Diffs, wheels and suspension not usually offered here would be included there, really bringing the best out of the answer to everything. Getting a fresh import these days will have benefits when it comes to rust as well - a lifetime spent in Japan has to be better for metal than here. This S-Special is the perfect example of a JDM-enhanced MX-5, with a viscous LSD, Bilstein dampers and BBS wheels included from factory. That it has been in the UK 20 years, yet still looks this good and has covered just 72,000 miles, points to considerate use. Still cheaper than some UK cars, too…
Honda S660, 2016, 32k, £15,990
Maybe there should be a Type R here: Civic, NSX, Accord and Integra all had red ‘H’ variants not sold here, all adored by fans in the UK who know their DC5 from their CL7. But one look at the adorable S660 is enough to have it included, the perfect reinterpretation of the classic kei car roadster. Would Honda have sold a few here? In the lean mid-'10s, surely: the tiny running costs of a 660cc triple, the engagement of a manual gearbox and the unique design would have charmed a few. Certainly a few have been intrigued over the years, because there are plenty of imports for sale on PH, from less than £15k. It won’t be fast and it won’t be furious, but an S660 is guaranteed fun - and that’s more important. This 2016 car has modest mileage, a Spoon exhaust and upgraded suspension. A pop to the shops will never be the same again.
summary: Japanese Domestic Market (JDM) cars have a rich history in the UK, driven by media like magazines and video games, as well as grey imports. While some models eventually received official UK releases, many of the best and rarest versions remained exclusive to Japan. Today, both classic and contemporary JDM vehicles—ranging from high-end performance icons to affordable roadsters—remain highly prized by enthusiasts.
key_points: A 2001 Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VII RS with 10k miles is listed for £49,990 as a raw, non-UK-market model.
The 2013 Subaru Impreza STI Type RA NBR Challenge, limited to 200 units, is available with under 20,000 miles for £44,985.
A 1996 Toyota Supra RZ-S demonstrates the model's transformation into a famous tuner car, priced at £68,000 with over 100,000 miles.
A JUN Auto-built 1990 Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) producing nearly 800hp is offered at £59,995 with 27k miles.
Affordable JDM options are available, such as a 1993 Mazda Eunos Roadster S-Special for £11,995 and a 2016 Honda S660 for £15,990.

title: ‘I am proud’: The high street family business still going strong after 80 years
author: Joe Harbert
content:
UK regional news website of the year
Surrounded by turntables, amplifiers and speakers, Geoff Mathews is still behind the counter of the family shop he first joined as a young man.
Now 74, he works alongside his sons Sam, 45, and Daniel, 48 – the third generation of a business that has survived huge changes in technology, shopping habits and the high street itself.
But Soundcraft Hi-Fi’s story began 80 years ago and more than 10 miles away, when Geoff’s father Victor opened a very different kind of shop in Hythe.
The family business dates back to 1946, when Victor, who had served as a photographer during the Second World War, launched Photocraft in Hythe High Street.
Selling cameras, lenses, telescopes and binoculars, it moved to Ashford in 1960, with Geoff joining his father behind the counter 12 years later.
“Back then, customers would visit us on a Friday to buy a camera, bring the film back to us to be developed on the Monday, and then come in on the Wednesday to collect it,” he told KentOnline.
“But the photography business was becoming more and more driven by price, and there were companies out there like Dixons who were hard to compete with.”
As tastes and technology changed, Photocraft branched into audio equipment and became Photocraft Hi-Fi, selling photography and sound equipment side-by-side.
“We made the transition to audio at a time when rock music was becoming prolific in the 1980s, with The Who, Pink Floyd, and Led Zeppelin,” Geoff said.
“That was the driving force when people wanted to record, recreate, and listen to the same songs.
“We always had an interest in radio and receiving radio from international stations, and customers also enjoyed turntables at a time when there were several record shops in Ashford.”
With the camera trade becoming increasingly competitive, the family eventually left photography behind altogether and, in the early 1990s, the business became Soundcraft Hi-Fi.
Today, it remains in Ashford’s Lower High Street, specialising in high-end audio equipment and turning over about £1 million a year.
“When I started the high street was very different, but when you fast forward people still want to buy the newest equipment.”
Geoff has added a home cinema to the shop so customers can experience equipment before buying it, while Arcam and Naim streaming products are its bestsellers, with about three turntables sold each week.
“Creating that immersive sound experience is what we try to do here,” he added.
“So we're selling and servicing high-end world class products and still telling the same story, but with more quality.
“We sell assembled turntables, but part of our business is to custom-build them so I can take a Linn turntable someone bought in 1979 and bring it up to the same specification you would buy today.”
But surviving for eight decades has meant adapting to more than changing musical tastes and technology.
Geoff says Brexit, the growth of online shopping and changes to Ashford town centre have all made trading more difficult, revealing Soundcraft could soon leave its long-standing central location.
Asked about the biggest challenges facing the business today, he said: “Coming out of the EU is probably the worst thing that ever happened to us as it slowed up the supply chain.
“It fundamentally changed our market because it meant that the delivery times were extended and distribution has become more centralised to Europe.
“Our whole high street is also harder to trade in now with all the road closures, the creation of the Designer Outlet, and the destruction of Park Mall.
“We want to continue being a destination store, so we’re more likely than not moving out of the town centre soon.
“The competition is also much more intense because of Amazon and eBay, so we don’t have people queuing outside the door.
"But we adapt as best as we can and have a good website - about one-third of our sales are online now.
“Of course, our business is very high on referrals and we spend more time going out to customers’ homes.”
Among those who have remained loyal to the shop through its changing guises is historian Steve Salter, from Kennington, who has been visiting since the early 1980s.
“I always come in to see what the latest equipment and audio is,” he said.
“It’s a success story because it’s developed with the times and is one of Kent’s leading audio specialists.
“Over the years, I’ve bought amplifiers, CD players, speakers, and even things when they were a photography business.”
Eight decades after Victor Mathews opened Photocraft in Hythe, the cameras and rolls of film have been replaced by turntables, speakers and streaming systems – but the family behind the counter remains the same.
“I am proud,” Geoff said. “I never expected my two boys to both be here alongside me today.”
summary: Soundcraft Hi-Fi is a family-run business in Ashford that has survived for 80 years by adapting from photography to high-end audio equipment. Currently run by Geoff Mathews and his two sons, the shop has evolved through changing technologies, music trends, and shopping habits. Despite challenges such as Brexit, online competition, and local town centre changes, the business continues to thrive through custom builds, home visits, and online sales.
key_points: The business was originally founded as a photography shop called Photocraft in 1946 by Victor Mathews.
It transitioned into selling audio equipment in the 1980s and eventually became Soundcraft Hi-Fi in the early 1990s.
The shop is now run by Geoff Mathews and his sons, Sam and Daniel, representing three generations.
Current challenges include Brexit supply chain issues, online competition from Amazon and eBay, and local town centre changes.
About one-third of sales are now online, and the business also focuses on custom-building equipment and home visits.

title: Lexar’s Muse is an ultra-slim portable SSD that’s less than 4mm thick
author: Andrew Liszewski
content:
Following the lead of companies like Xteink, Lexar is the latest to sacrifice a USB-C port in the pursuit of slimming down its hardware.
Lexar’s Muse is an ultra-slim portable SSD that’s less than 4mm thick
You can slim down your portable storage if you don’t mind dealing with a proprietary USB-C cable.
![lexarmuse1](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/lexarmuse1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.042301184433164%2C100%2C99.915397631134&w=2400)
![lexarmuse1](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/lexarmuse1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.042301184433164%2C100%2C99.915397631134&w=2400)
When the Lexar Muse Ultra-Slim Portable SSD launches later this year in 512GB and 1TB capacities it will be one of the slimmest you can buy. At its thickest point in the middle it measures just 3.8mm, but that tapers to only 1mm at the edges thanks to high-density NAND stacking and a “custom ultra-thin PCB architecture” inside. But performance remains solid with read speeds up to 1,050MB/s and write speeds maxing out at 1,000MB/s. That’s fast enough to record 4K Apple ProRes video at up to 120fps when connected to a compatible iPhone.
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/lexarmuse4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The downside is that without a standard USB-C port, you’ll need to rely on — and make sure not to lose — Lexar’s proprietary SnapLink cable that magnetically attaches to a pogo-pin connector on the side of the drive. The company doesn’t specify the strength of the magnets, but this approach also means there’s an increased risk of the cable being accidentally knocked off during a file transfer. And if you are using the Muse to record videos through your phone, you’ll need to slip it into an included magnetic sleeve in order to mount it to the back of your device, adding quite a bit of thickness in the process.
summary: Lexar has announced the Muse, an ultra-slim portable SSD measuring less than 4mm thick that is set to launch later this year in 512GB and 1TB capacities. The drive achieves its thin profile by using high-density NAND stacking and a custom PCB architecture while maintaining read speeds up to 1,050MB/s and write speeds up to 1,000MB/s. However, to achieve this slim design, Lexar sacrificed a standard USB-C port in favor of a proprietary magnetic SnapLink cable.
key_points: The Lexar Muse portable SSD measures 3.8mm at its thickest point and tapers to 1mm at the edges.
It will be available in 512GB and 1TB capacities when it launches later this year.
The drive delivers read speeds up to 1,050MB/s and write speeds up to 1,000MB/s.
It lacks a standard USB-C port and requires a proprietary magnetic SnapLink cable for connection.
Mounting the drive to a phone for video recording requires an included magnetic sleeve, which adds thickness.

title: LEGO PlayStation officially revealed with hidden dioramas
author: Dylan McLaren
content:
The LEGO Group has revealed a nearly 2,000-piece LEGO PlayStation model, and it’s packed full of references to the iconic console’s history.
Nearly 32 years after its original release, the first PlayStation is being immortalised in LEGO form next month with the release of 72306 PlayStation. The set recreates the revolutionary 1994 console, complete with its controller and a collection of Easter eggs hidden throughout the build.
Price: £139.99 / $179.99 / €159.99 Pieces: 1,911 Release date: October 1, 2026
![](https://www.brickfanatics.com/public/storage/uploads/efe2e654-a1ff-4be4-af6f-16064c0b1166.jpg)
72306 PlayStation contains 1,911 pieces and recreates the original Sony console from the 1990s. The build captures the distinctive design of the PlayStation while also incorporating a surprising amount of functionality, making it more than just a display model.
The controller uses printed elements to recreate the iconic Square, Triangle, Circle and Cross buttons, and can be plugged into the slot on the front of the console. Pressing a button also opens the top of the build, allowing you to look inside without having to take the model apart.
Priced at £139.99 / $179.99 / €159.99, the set opens up to reveal two smaller dioramas based on classic PlayStation games.
The most recognisable of the two is a miniature Gran Turismo track, which can slide in and out of the side of the console. On the other side is a diorama based on Ape Escape, complete with one of the game’s distinctive red or blue monkeys.
72306 PlayStation will be available for LEGO Insiders from October 1, before becoming widely available on October 4.
Support the work that Brick Fanatics does by purchasing your LEGO using our affiliate links. Thanks!
summary: The LEGO Group has announced a 1,911-piece LEGO PlayStation set recreating the 1994 console and its controller. Set to release in October 2026, the model features hidden dioramas based on Gran Turismo and Ape Escape. The set will be priced at £139.99 / $179.99 / €159.99.
key_points: The set consists of 1,911 pieces and releases in October 2026.
It features a buildable PlayStation console and controller with printed button elements.
Pressing a button opens the top of the console to reveal hidden interior features.
The model includes slide-out dioramas based on Gran Turismo and Ape Escape.

title: GTA 6 Netflix preview causes PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales to jump in the UK
author: Sophie McEvoy
content:
PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S console sales increased in the UK following last week's Grand Theft Auto 6 reveal on Netflix.
According to The Games Business, Nielsen IQ data shows PS5 sales rose by 33% and Xbox console sales grew by 34%.
PS5 Pro consoles are selling out nationwide, and retailers including Argos and Smyths Toys now only have base models available.
Despite a significant jump in the run-up to GTA 6's launch in November, alongside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in October, Newzoo's Ronan Patrick said that it expects to see "an uptick in the install base but nothing particularly massive."
"The PS5 in inflation-adjusted terms is 67% more expensive [than at launch], and Xbox is twice as expensive," said Patrick.
"It's important to remember that the lion's share of time is often spent on older titles, and the closest analogy we have to a hardware shock is during the 2020-2021 GPU shortage, and you didn't see engagement or revenue being taken off course. You basically saw a reallocation of spend into software."
VGC reports that UK hardware sales are down 14.4% year-on-year, primarily due to a 32% decline in PS5 sales. Xbox Series X|S sales have increased by 3.1%.
The extended GTA 6 preview was Netflix's most-viewed title last week, reaching 31.1 million views in four days. On YouTube, the preview received 22 million views in one week.
Sensor Tower data shows that Netflix's US mobile viewership increased by 35% hour-over-hour during the premiere.
summary: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S console sales in the UK increased following a Grand Theft Auto 6 preview on Netflix. Nielsen IQ data showed a 33% rise in PS5 sales and a 34% increase for Xbox consoles. Meanwhile, overall UK hardware sales remain down year-on-year, and industry analysts expect only a moderate boost to the install base due to higher inflation-adjusted console prices.
key_points: UK sales for PlayStation 5 rose by 33% and Xbox consoles grew by 34% following the GTA 6 preview.
PS5 Pro consoles are selling out nationwide, leaving retailers with only base models.
Despite the sales jump, overall UK hardware sales are down 14.4% year-on-year.
The extended GTA 6 preview became Netflix's most-viewed title, reaching 31.1 million views in four days.
